behavioral_notes.element: product.wishlist (per partner / per website) + add/remove routes (controllers/main.py, models/product_wishlist.py)
behavioral_notes.observation: The wishlist is one product.wishlist row per (product_id, partner_id) — enforced by a UNIQUE(product_id, partner_id) SQL constraint — carrying website_id (ondelete='cascade', required), the pricelist_id and the price snapshotted when the product was added. /shop/wishlist/add (jsonrpc, public) browses the product.product, reads its variant price via _get_combination_info_variant()['price'] and calls product.wishlist._add_to_wishlist(...) to create the row; /shop/wishlist (http, public) renders the website_sale_wishlist.product_wishlist template with current() items; /shop/wishlist/remove/<wish_id> (jsonrpc) unlinks one entry; /shop/wishlist/get_product_ids (jsonrpc, readonly) returns the current product ids so the storefront can mark already-wishlisted products. Not visible in metadata.

Anonymous visitors are detected via request.website.is_public_user(): for them the wishlist is created sudo() with partner_id=False and the new wish.id is appended to request.session['wishlist_ids'] (session-scoped list), so guests get a wishlist without a partner. For a logged-in user the row is owned by request.env.user.partner_id and scoped to request.website.id. product.wishlist.current() returns session-id rows (sudo) for public users and partner+website rows otherwise, then filters out items whose product template is not website_published or fails _is_add_to_cart_possible(). Not visible in metadata.

res.users._check_credentials is overridden so that on successful login, if request.session holds wishlist_ids, _check_wishlist_from_session() runs: it loads the session's partner-less wishes and the user's existing wishes, drops session wishes whose product already exists for the partner (unlink, avoiding the UNIQUE(product_id, partner_id) clash), reassigns the remaining session wishes to the user's partner_id, and pops wishlist_ids from the session. This is the guest->customer hand-off that persists an anonymous wishlist across login. Not visible in metadata.

product.wishlist stores the variant price at add-time (price Monetary, help='Price of the product when it has been added in the wishlist') together with the pricelist_id and a currency_id related to website_id.currency_id. Keeping the original price alongside the live computed price lets the wishlist page compare the as-saved price with the current price (price-drop / changed-price indication) per stored pricelist/currency. Not visible in metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: add-to-cart from wishlist + autovacuum GC (frontend interactions + product.wishlist._gc_sessions)
behavioral_notes.observation: The wishlist page is an action surface, not just a saved list: its public.interactions (add_product_to_wishlist_button, product_detail, product_wishlist, wishlist_navbar) let the shopper add a wishlisted product into the website_sale cart (move-to-cart) and remove it, driving conversion back into the /shop/cart flow. Stale guest wishlists are cleaned by @api.autovacuum _gc_sessions, which unlinks partner-less rows older than ~5 weeks (create_date threshold) so orphaned session wishlists do not accumulate. Not visible in metadata.

6 JS files, 0 OWL components, 4 public.interactions registry adds (add_product_to_wishlist_button, product_detail, product_wishlist, wishlist_navbar); 3 entries in web.assets_frontend plus a web.assets_tests bundle and a website.website_builder_assets bundle (wishlist-page grid layout options exposed in the website builder). The wishlist UX is delivered as website public interactions over QWeb templates, not backend OWL views.

it_architecture.application: website_sale_wishlist (Shopper's Wishlist; storefront engagement add-on on website_sale)
information_flows: depends: website_sale (storefront, public users, product catalog, cart)
inbound: website public user / portal customer -> /shop/wishlist/add -> product.wishlist row (session-scoped for guests, partner-scoped for logged-in)
side-effect: res.users login (_check_credentials) -> _check_wishlist_from_session merges anonymous session wishes onto the partner
side-effect: wishlist page move-to-cart -> website_sale cart (/shop/cart) -> feeds the eCommerce browse-to-order flow
side-effect: @api.autovacuum _gc_sessions purges stale partner-less (guest) wishlists (~5 weeks)

capabilities: Save Products to a Wishlist (add / remove)
Persist Wishlist per Customer and per Website
value_streams: Save-for-later: shopper marks a product -> product.wishlist entry (guest session or partner) -> returns later via /shop/wishlist
Wishlist-to-cart: wishlist page -> add to website_sale cart -> joins the eCommerce browse-to-order flow (conversion)
policies: ir.rule 'See own Wishlist' (portal + internal user limited to partner_id = user.partner_id)
4 ACLs: public/portal/user access on product.wishlist (public read-only, portal/user CRUD)
UNIQUE(product_id, partner_id) constraint — one wishlist entry per product per owner
stakeholders: eCommerce Manager / Website Publisher (configures wishlist page layout)
metrics: product.wishlist row counts (saved demand / interest signal per product)

classification.apqc_category: 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services
classification.rationale: website_sale_wishlist is a storefront mediation/engagement feature of the website_sale value network: it lets the shared eCommerce platform remember each visitor's product interest (session-scoped for anonymous visitors, partner-scoped once logged in, merged on login) so the storefront can re-engage shoppers and convert saved interest into orders. Its value logic is network (Stabell & Fjeldstad): matchmaking/mediation over shared channel infrastructure that increases the value of the website_sale network by driving return visits and conversion (move-to-cart back into the browse-to-order flow), not a linear transform-inputs-to-output chain. It owns no order/document chain of its own; it decorates website_sale's catalog and cart. Activity is primary because it is a revenue- and customer-facing online merchandising/engagement capability on the sell-side channel, hence APQC 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services (eCommerce merchandising / customer engagement), not a back-office support function.

standard_capabilities: Add-to-wishlist button on product pages and product tiles
Anonymous session wishlist merged onto the customer on login
Wishlist page (/shop/wishlist) listing saved products with remove and add-to-cart
Price snapshot at add-time vs current price per stored pricelist/currency
Configurable wishlist page grid layout (columns, mobile columns, gap) via website builder
Automatic garbage-collection of stale guest wishlists (~5 weeks)
typical_fits: B2C save-for-later on a public storefront (guest or registered)
Customer returns, opens wishlist, moves an item into the cart
common_gaps: Wishlist sharing / public or social wishlists (not standard)
Multiple named wishlists / registries (gift registry) per customer
Automated price-drop or back-in-stock notification emails (only the price snapshot is stored; no mailing here)
Wishlist analytics / demand reporting dashboards beyond raw rows
